scope: Fourteen partial game studies including packaged-source Alpha Zoo research; gameplay remains unobserved.
method: Version-tagged upstream source snapshots with Git blob verification
Selected Java bytecode decompilation using CFR
Bounded executable entry-point disassembly; not recovered gameplay routines
Prince of Persia DAT resource-directory decoding with bounds checks
SimFarm resource-directory decoding and exact round-trip validation of 22 planar bitmap payloads
Fixed-record decoding of authored guidance in all 24 SimFarm crop files
Black & White supplied-disc inventory and gesture-focused primary documentation study
Black & White InstallShield extraction, complete gesture-template metadata decoding and isolated x86 recognizer probes
Alpha Zoo ASAR application extraction with bounds and declared integrity checks; packaged JavaScript inspection
limitations: Original binary behavior is not proven by reading upstream source or a modern reimplementation.
No game has been play-tested in this pilot; UI findings are code-level and UX remains unobserved.
Unrecognized or packed formats can conceal sprites, audio and models. Zero loose model files does not establish no models.
Widelands package extraction remains blocked; source evidence is available.

games.title: Widelands
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Requests become physical transfers
claims.finding: The economy pairs open requests with available supplies, checks that each is still valid, and starts transfers. Lowest-priority requests are deferred when higher-priority work exists.

flow.failure: Missing request or exhausted supply is skipped and reconsidered later.

claims.title: Routes belong to an economy
claims.finding: Route lookup requires both endpoint flags to belong to this economy and passes a cost cutoff to its router.

claims.title: Separate seeded generation fields
claims.finding: The map generator seeds a private RNG with the map number and builds separate random fields for elevation, terrain, resources and other map contents.

claims.title: Stopping respects production-cycle boundaries
claims.finding: program_act honors the stopped flag when the program instruction pointer is zero, unless the program explicitly ignores stopping. The source explains that interrupting later could consume inputs without producing output. set_stopped also rebalances ware and worker supply and publishes a building-change notification.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; no gameplay observation

claims.title: Output handling precedes the next production work
claims.finding: Pending produced wares are instantiated and assigned to a worker drop-off task before program work continues. Outstanding worker requests prevent normal production work from starting and put the worker into an idle retry. Basic unloading can still begin while staffing is incomplete.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; no gameplay observation

claims.title: Failed and skipped programs carry retry state
claims.finding: program_start consults the previous failure/skip timestamp and delays a restart until that timestamp plus Duration(10000). program_end records failed or skipped outcomes as nonproductive, while completion clears retry state, trains workers and records productive time. Nested program results propagate to the parent phase. This is static control-flow evidence, not an observed recovery scenario.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; no gameplay observation

claims.title: Bakery recipe links demand, inputs and two outputs
claims.finding: The Barbarian bakery defines one baker and input queues of six water and six wheat. Its main program skips when bread is not needed, consumes three of each input, sleeps for 20.8 seconds, then performs two 20-second working stages, each followed by a bread output. These are authored action durations; delivery overhead and observed throughput are not established.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Missing ingredients fail before input removal
claims.finding: ActConsume computes proposed consumption using local quantities. If required groups remain unmet, it builds ingredient-specific feedback and ends the program as failed before changing queue contents. Only the successful branch subtracts inputs and updates consumption statistics. ActProduce then hands pending output to the building worker; transport remains a separate step.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Demand combines district stock, storage policy and open requests
claims.finding: With a positive permanent target and at least one warehouse, the economy compares warehouse stock against the global target and a district share rounded upward. Local shortages can justify production even when global stock is sufficient, but local storage policy and preferred warehouses elsewhere can suppress that local need. Outside this branch, matching open requests determine demand, including when no warehouses exist. The production-site infinite-production setting bypasses the ware demand predicate.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Treat a stop as a defined boundary, preserve pending output handling, and expose staffing shortages and delayed retries as distinct states. This is a design inference from source, not implemented Ranch behavior.

games.nextPass: Demand predicate, bakery recipe and input-failure branches are now source-traced. Delivery completion, demand-target UI, runtime throughput and recovery remain unobserved. Installer remains unextracted. Advance to the next pilot subsystem while retaining these gaps.

games.title: Sim Farm
games.version: Acquired DOS package; exact build not established
games.sourceBasis: Original package inspection; no recovered gameplay source
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Main archive decoded into 151 resources
claims.finding: MEGADATA.IDX contains 152 fixed 20-byte records: 151 named payloads and an EOF boundary marker. Sixteen-byte name fields precede little-endian offsets; adjacent offsets delimit payloads. All payloads partition the 2,213,377-byte EEA archive exactly. Guidance sections in all 24 crop files are now decoded; their binary parameters remain unresolved.

claims.title: Voice resources are separate from drivers
claims.finding: The archive contains 25 .VOC resources with Creative Voice File signatures and eight .XMI-named resources. README.TXT separately identifies the 15 loose .ADV files as Miles sound-card drivers. Audio playback and XMI event decoding remain untested.

claims.title: Original executable entry inspected
claims.finding: The DOS MZ header and a bounded entry-point instruction listing are recorded for SIMFARM.EXE. This is disassembly of startup code, not recovered crop simulation code.

claims.title: 22 planar interface images decoded
claims.finding: All 22 .BMP-named resources fit an eight-byte header followed by four contiguous bitplanes. Width is the stored row-byte count multiplied by eight. Decoding and repacking every image reproduces the original payload exactly. A visual inspection of weather.bmp confirms legible labels and aligned borders; these are static assets, not captured gameplay.
claims.basis: binary decoding + round-trip validation + visual inspection

claims.title: Weather data is stored in twelve numeric tables
claims.finding: Four rain, four temperature and four wind resources each contain 60 rows of four integer values. Their structure and ranges are recorded. Units, calendar mapping, randomness and the game routines consuming these values have not been established.
claims.basis: parsed packaged data; runtime interpretation unresolved

claims.title: Weather has a dedicated comparison panel
claims.finding: The decoded weather panel reserves areas for temperature, rainfall, wind direction/speed, evaporation, current weather and a five-day forecast. This verifies an authored information layout; dynamic values and interactive behavior were not observed.
claims.basis: visual inspection of decoded interface artwork

claims.title: Messages distinguish blocked farm actions
claims.finding: The packaged message table includes separate feedback for insufficient operating funds, occupied fields, invalid placement and unmet plowing/planting prerequisites. This establishes authored failure feedback, not proof that the corresponding simulation branches execute correctly.

claims.title: Crop files combine binary data and framed guidance
claims.finding: All 24 CRP files are 5,890 bytes. A crop name begins at offset 5,376; an unmapped parameter region precedes two fixed-record text sections. Their line endings, padding and seven detailed guidance fields decode consistently across every file. The binary prefix and parameter meanings remain unresolved.
claims.basis: static decoding of authored crop guidance; runtime unverified

evidence.path: cropDecoding: file hashes, byte offsets, text framing and derived guidance

claims.title: Crop guidance distinguishes recurring harvests from replanting
claims.finding: Authored guidance says almonds, apples, grapes and oranges do not need replanting after each harvest; the other 20 crops do. Each crop also has separate pest, weed and disease resistance labels, rain-day guidance, a temperature criterion and storage guidance. These are packaged descriptions, not verified executable rules. Temperature guidance uses chill hours, degree days or freeze avoidance; rain labels span 2 to 14 days, with their runtime interpretation unresolved.
claims.basis: static decoding of authored crop guidance; runtime unverified

evidence.path: cropDecoding: file hashes, byte offsets, text framing and derived guidance

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Explain blocked actions by their specific prerequisite, and compare current conditions with a near-term forecast. These lessons come from packaged presentation assets; simulation execution remains unverified.

games.nextPass: Map CRP binary parameters and artwork framing; trace executable consumers of weather and crop guidance. Crop text is decoded, but actual growth, harvest, storage and replanting behavior remains unverified. Resolve Widelands extraction independently.

games.title: OpenTTD
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Cargo payment depends on time and distance
claims.finding: The default delivery calculation combines cargo quantity, distance, the cargo payment rate and a time factor. Cargo-specific callbacks can override it. The default time factor declines after cargo-specific transit thresholds.

flow.state: Quantity, distance, transit periods, cargo type
flow.failure: An invalid cargo specification returns zero.

claims.title: Seed before world construction
claims.finding: World generation sets the RNG seed before landscape generation, then builds world contents including industries, objects and trees. An explicitly requested new seed is obtained separately.

claims.title: Delivery needs an accepting destination
claims.finding: Delivery checks industries near the station, skips the source industry, and looks for matching accepted cargo. Being physically near an industry is not sufficient by itself.

claims.title: Acceptance limits how much delivery earns
claims.finding: Industry delivery skips temporary refusals and stations that do not satisfy an exclusive-supplier restriction. Incoming stock is capped at 65,535 units per accepted-cargo slot. DeliverGoods uses accepted quantity for statistics and transport income, with a station always-accepted flag able to accept the full amount independently of industry acceptance. Eligible subsidies then modify the calculated income.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Cargo arrival and production are separate stages
claims.finding: TriggerIndustryProduction distinguishes callback-driven industries from default conversion. An arrival callback runs when supported; a periodic-production callback instead leaves this branch to mark the industry view dirty. The default path converts waiting inputs with configured input/output multipliers divided by 256, clamps output stock to uint16, and clears processed input stock. Cargo-received randomisation and animation triggers follow. This is source control flow, not observed production timing.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Lost station acceptance changes unloading by order
claims.finding: When station acceptance disappears while delivery-marked cargo is unloading, explicit Transfer or Unload orders reassign that cargo to transfer. Other orders reassign it to keep aboard; reserved cargo may be returned to prevent exceeding capacity. That keep branch sets an internal activity flag so loading is retried next cycle, even if nothing physically unloaded. This is a station-acceptance recovery branch, not proof of how every industry-level refusal is handled.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Transfer credit is distinct from company income
claims.finding: PayTransfer computes journey income minus previous feeder shares, scales it by the feeder-payment percentage, and accumulates virtual transfer profit without adding route income. PayFinalDelivery adds delivery income to route profit but subtracts prior feeder shares from the final vehicle's visual profit. CargoPayment finalization applies route profit to company money, combines visual delivery and transfer amounts for vehicle profit, and chooses transfer-specific or ordinary income animation. These are source accounting paths, not observed balances or UI.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Packet splits preserve allocated feeder credit
claims.finding: CargoPacket::Split first checks allocation availability and returns null before modifying the original if no packet can be allocated. On success it assigns GetFeederShare(new_size) to the new packet and subtracts that exact amount and cargo count from the original. The new packet retains transit age, source, travelled distance and routing fields. Merge adds both count and feeder share before deleting the merged packet; Reduce subtracts the removed portion's share. Call-site validity and rounding inside GetFeederShare remain separate questions.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Cargo merging checks identity and packet capacity
claims.finding: Both vehicle and station cargo lists compare source coordinates, transit age, first station and source identity for merge compatibility. TryMerge additionally requires the combined count to stay within MAX_COUNT, defined as UINT16_MAX (65,535). The partial feeder-share accessor computes stored share multiplied by the selected count divided by packet count. These source checks constrain merging; list grouping, all call-site preconditions and extreme arithmetic behavior are not established by this inspection.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Show route profitability as the consequence of quantity, travel time and acceptance, rather than as an unexplained money increment.

games.nextPass: Packet sharing formula and merge guards are source-traced. All caller constraints, arithmetic extremes and industry-refusal packet handling remain open. Move to another pilot subsystem next; runtime balances and visuals remain unverified.

games.title: Freeciv
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Food reserves drive growth and famine
claims.finding: city_populate adds food surplus to reserves. Reaching the growth threshold can increase size, with a recent-plague check. Negative reserves first consider food-upkeep units; otherwise famine reduces population. Player notices and script signals are part of these branches.

flow.state: Food reserve, surplus, granary size, supported units
flow.output: Growth, upkeep-unit loss or population loss
flow.failure: Recent plague can prevent growth; negative food triggers famine handling.

claims.title: Unbuildable work has explicit policy
claims.finding: The worklist code distinguishes postponing an unavailable target from purging it, and checks different requirement vectors for units and improvements.

claims.title: Rules are exposed as data files
claims.finding: The installed-content extraction contains 676 .ruleset files, 133 .spec files, 2,752 PNG files and 1,302 SVG files. These are file counts across the package, not unique gameplay entity counts.

claims.title: Blocked work can wait, signal scripts or be removed
claims.finding: The always-postpone policy returns before requirement-specific removal logic. Otherwise, missing required technology emits need_tech feedback/signals and is postponed, while a failed negative technology requirement marks the item for removal. The requirement evaluator checks whether scripts removed the city before proceeding. If it cannot identify a blocking requirement, it defaults to removal. Worklist scanning also rechecks city existence after script-sensitive work. These are source branches, not observed queue recovery.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Worklist selection upgrades and removes entries explicitly
claims.finding: The worklist scanner can replace a target with its unit or building upgrade and notifies the player. Purged entries emit a never-buildable signal, recheck city existence, decrement the scan index and remove the entry. After a successful selection, it calls change_build_target and removes the selected entry at index i-1. This distinguishes consuming a selected queue entry from discarding an unavailable one; it does not establish runtime behavior for every ruleset or script.
claims.basis: pinned original release-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Classic Granary separates prerequisites from food effects
claims.finding: In the pinned classic ruleset, the Granary requires player technology Pottery, declares build_cost 40 and upkeep 1, and separately contributes 50 to Growth_Food and 50 to Shrink_Food when present in the city. The engine obtains each combined city bonus and clamps its savings percentage to 0–100. The building contribution is not necessarily the total city effect: other effects can contribute. This is configuration and source evidence, not confirmation that every game uses the classic ruleset.
claims.basis: pinned ruleset plus original engine-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Growth caps reserves; famine resets them
claims.finding: After adding food surplus, city_populate checks the growth threshold or celebration growth before checking negative reserves. Recent plague caps food at the current threshold and blocks this growth attempt. Successful ordinary growth caps existing food at the new-size granary capacity times the combined savings percentage; celebration instead caps it at full new-size capacity. Blocked growth uses an aqueduct-loss formula and does not increase reserves. On negative reserves, the first supported unit with positive food upkeep is passed to upkeep_kill_unit; if the city still exists, food is reset for its current size, then the function returns even if the helper reported no kill. With no such unit, food resets for size minus one and city_reduce_size handles famine population loss. Shrink resets assign capacity times savings, rather than taking a minimum. Helper internals and runtime outcomes remain unverified.
claims.basis: pinned original engine-source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Upkeep failure can protect a unit from removal
claims.finding: Without an eligible AAPC_UNIT_UPKEEP action auto performer, upkeep_kill_unit returns false before any forced wipe. Otherwise it executes upkeep actions, optionally wipes a surviving unit, and returns whether the original unit ID is no longer alive. Thus the caller cannot assume every food-upkeep unit is destroyed.
claims.basis: Original pinned source inspection; not decompilation or gameplay observation

claims.title: Population loss repairs assignments and guards script-driven destruction
claims.finding: Zero loss returns true. Loss at least equal to city size emits city_destroyed, checks whether the city still exists before removing it, then returns false. A surviving city loses size, updates borders, caps food to its new capacity, removes specialists before workers, refreshes citizens and worker allocation, and refreshes trade partners. If a reason is supplied, city_size_change is emitted and the return value checks whether scripts left the city alive.
claims.basis: Original pinned source inspection; not decompilation or gameplay observation

claims.title: Classic starvation protects evacuation units
claims.finding: The pinned classic cities ruleset protects the EvacuateFirst unit-type flag from food-upkeep removal, provides no food action list, and enables food_wipe. The ruleset loader maps this configuration to the food-specific upkeep auto performer and the engine wipe setting. In conjunction with the helper early return, protection is checked before forced wiping. Shield upkeep uses a different policy: three ordered actions and no final wipe. These are classic configuration and source branches, not observed play or a rule for every ruleset. The two classic unit declarations carrying EvacuateFirst are Leader and Barbarian Leader. Both also declare NoHome and uk_food=0. Therefore the protected-unit helper branch does not by itself demonstrate a reachable classic famine scenario for these units: city_populate filters for positive actual food upkeep. Effects and alternate rulesets require further tracing.
claims.basis: pinned classic configuration and original source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Forced-action selection and execution have distinct outcomes
claims.finding: Selection returns the first performer in cause-iteration order whose requirements are active with RPT_CERTAIN, using actor owner, tile, unit, unit type, output and action context. Execution selects again, acquires targets, then iterates alternatives for unit actors. Each target-kind branch checks action eligibility before invoking unit_perform_action. A successful action immediately returns its action descriptor; this is not a survival guarantee. After an unsuccessful attempt, actor death returns null, preventing further attempts. Exhausting alternatives also returns null. Consequently null alone does not distinguish no performer, no successful action, or actor death.
claims.basis: pinned original source inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Unit removal prioritizes cargo rescue before secondary losses
claims.finding: wipe_unit delegates to wipe_unit_full, which unloads the doomed unit and its cargo, classifies cargo by unload ability and terrain survival, then removes the carrier. It processes helpless cargo before imperiled cargo, prioritizing EvacuateFirst or GameLoss within each group. Non-helpless cargo can seek another transport; only EvacuateFirst receives the teleport fallback. Unrescued cargo is subsequently removed with transport-loss reason. Starvation increments units_lost, whereas disbanded/used units increment units_used. This describes shared removal branches; it does not prove a food-upkeep carrier can encounter every branch in the classic ruleset.
claims.basis: pinned original source inspection; runtime unobserved

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Keep growth, shortages and blocked production explainable through explicit state and reason-specific messages.

games.nextPass: Shortage and removal dispatch now have a bounded static trace. Requirement evaluator internals, individual action effects, transport/teleport helpers and runtime remain partial or unexamined; next deepen another pilot game.

games.title: Mindustry
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Capacity constrains production
claims.finding: GenericCrafter advances progress when efficient, emits liquids within remaining capacity, crafts at completed progress and attempts to dump outputs. Liquid fullness can limit progress; options alter how excess output is treated. The inspected method also appears in the decompiled downloaded class.

flow.failure: Insufficient output capacity can limit progress; behavior depends on liquid-output options.

claims.title: Sector identity controls seeded generation
claims.finding: PlanetGenerator seeds its random generator from sector ID, seed offset and base seed. Its noise helper projects sector coordinates into 3D before sampling simplex noise.

claims.title: Favorites are persistent selection state
claims.finding: The HUD toggles named block favorites, saves them in settings and builds the selection list with favorites first. This establishes implementation behavior, not an observed usability result.

claims.title: Bytecode, schematics and maps are distinct
claims.finding: The extracted JAR contains 4,486 .class files, 210 .msch files and 114 .msav files. Five selected top-level classes were decompiled with CFR 0.152; this is not decompilation of every class.

claims.title: Conveyor motion propagates spacing constraints upstream
claims.finding: updateTile processes items from the forward end backward, clamps movement against the next item minus itemSpace, and applies a downstream limit derived from an aligned conveyor minitem. Motion uses speed times edelta. This traces local spacing and blocking, not whole-network throughput or conservation.

claims.title: Conveyor transfer checks receiver acceptance before local removal
claims.finding: pass requires a nonnull item and next building, same team, and receiver acceptItem. It invokes receiver handleItem and returns true; updateTile removes its local item only on that success. A rejected transfer remains on the belt. No transaction rollback or exception guarantee was established.

claims.title: Side loading uses stricter spacing and inserts halfway along the belt
claims.finding: acceptItem rejects full capacity or an absent facing edge. Direction-zero input needs minitem>=itemSpace; side input needs minitem>0.7. A rotating source that is also the next building is rejected. handleItem inserts direction-zero input at y=0 and side input at y=0.5 with lateral offset. External callers must honor acceptance; handleItem itself only checks capacity before using the facing edge.

claims.title: Conveyor saves quantize positions and retain legacy decoding
claims.finding: Revision 1 writes item count, short item ID and signed-byte encodings of lateral and forward position. read consumes every declared entry but stores only up to capacity; revision 0 decodes an older packed integer representation. It invokes updateTile after loading, so deserialization includes an update rather than only field assignment. This is not a runtime save/load round-trip or malformed-input validation result.

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Tie visible machine activity to simulated warmup and blocked outputs; save quick-choice preferences independently of world state.

games.nextPass: Local conveyor movement, acceptance and serialization are partially traced. Network conservation, cache invalidation and runtime outcomes remain unexamined.

games.title: The Powder Toy
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Material definitions specify physical behavior
claims.finding: The WATR element declares advection, air loss, gravity, weight and temperature transitions. Its high-temperature transition is configured at internal temperature 373.0 to WTRV. These are game parameters, not a claim of scientific accuracy.

claims.title: Visuals are computed from particle properties
claims.finding: The particle renderer starts from each element’s color and a flat pixel mode, then supports glow, blur and fire modes with fallback behavior based on enabled rendering modes.

claims.title: Air is a separate field
claims.finding: The inspected air update works over a grid of heat and velocity values and samples neighboring cells through a kernel, with blocked-neighbor handling.

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Distinguish simulated material state from its rendering mode; a rich procedural image can come from a compact set of rules.

games.nextPass: Trace brush input, element update ordering and save format. Observe how overlays explain temperature/pressure. The three-file package is not proof that no art is embedded.

games.title: Endless Sky
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Ships are composed from layered sprites
claims.finding: The engine draws a ship as a stack that can include hardpoints, engine flares and externally carried fighters. Cloaking affects sprite composition. This is a source-level rendering finding, not evidence that original art was authored in 2D.

claims.title: The map changes meaning with the selected metric
claims.finding: Map nodes are filtered by knowledge/access and colored from the selected criterion. In the commodity branch, prices are normalized against the commodity’s low and high values.

claims.title: Calculation and drawing have separate paths
claims.finding: Go queues CalculateStep and changes the calculation buffer; Draw separately advances its UI counter and draws the background with camera velocity. Paused simulation time is explicitly checked.

claims.title: Mission offers and acceptance have separate eligibility checks
claims.finding: CanOffer checks context-specific source filters, offer/failure conditions, repeat limits and feasibility of offer/accept/decline/defer actions. CanAccept separately checks acceptance conditions, offer/accept action feasibility and available space. CreateMissions skips job templates when the current planet lacks a job-board service and routes jobs separately from other offered missions. This distinguishes an offer from a capacity-validated acceptance; UI handling is not yet traced.

claims.title: Procedural missions begin failed and become valid only after instantiation
claims.finding: Instantiate builds a new result with hasFailed=true, copies authored settings and selects locations from filters. Missing filtered waypoints, stopovers or destinations return the failed result. A missing or invalid fixed destination falls back to the current planet when available. The normal successful path substitutes display text and clears hasFailed at the end. CreateMissions excludes failed instantiated results before adding them to available lists. This is authored-template instantiation, not proof of procedural story generation; selection distributions and all nested action behavior remain unexamined.

claims.title: Player mission capacity includes reclaimable commodity space and extra crew bunks
claims.finding: HasSpace(PlayerInfo) compares mission cargo with free cargo plus commodity cargo, and passengers with free bunks plus flagship crew above required crew. The Ship overload instead tests strictly free cargo and bunks. Subsequent sale/unloading and crew-dismissal operations remain untraced.

claims.title: Default cargo-job payment scales with route and payload
claims.finding: A bare payment directive adds 150 to paymentMultiplier. GameAction instantiation computes payment + (jumps + 1) * payload * paymentMultiplier. Mission instantiation defines payload as cargoSize + 10*passengers. Thus the inspected Cargo [0] template, which specifies bare completion payment, derives its reward from generated cargo quantity and calculated jumps. MissionAction instantiates the action before dialog substitution and preserves completion-payment text across later actions. Route calculation and actual credit transfer remain outside this bounded trace.

claims.title: Landing resolves failure before completion and makes one extra dependency pass
claims.finding: StepMissions first reconciles destroyed mission NPC ships and executes each mission stopover action. It then tests failure before completion; otherwise, arrivals can run visit actions. A second pass checks failure/completion again because one mission action may change another mission. This is two passes, not a general fixed-point solver. Nonunique visible jobs aggregate unfinished-arrival dialogs. The final sweep removes cargo/passenger references absent from the active mission list.

claims.title: Mission removal leaves the active list before callbacks and cleans cargo afterward
claims.finding: RemoveMission moves the mission into doneMissions before executing its trigger, preserving lifetime for dialogs and preventing a self-failing callback from finding it in the active list again. It then removes mission cargo from the player hold and each ship. Mission::Do updates fail/abort counters before checking action feasibility, so an unavailable fail action does not prevent failure accounting. Abort without its own action uses the fail action for compatibility. Complete counters are updated only after the action feasibility check. This traces normal control flow; exceptions, persistence and UI dialog lifecycle remain unexamined.

claims.title: Deadlines mark failure after the due date; landing resolves removal
claims.finding: CheckDeadline marks a mission failed only when it has a deadline strictly earlier than today and has not already been marked failed. Equality with the due date does not trigger this check. PlayerInfo checks deadlines during its date-update loop, emits a message for newly expired visible missions, and skips daily actions for failed missions. The inspected landing path later prioritizes failure removal. This traces the named paths, not every possible failure-removal caller.

claims.title: Arrival is insufficient when mission cargo remains in another system
claims.finding: CanComplete requires the destination or matching completion filter and IsSatisfied. Satisfaction checks remaining waypoints/stopovers, completion conditions, action feasibility, NPC success and nonoptional timers. It then blocks completion for mission passengers or any mission cargo entry on an out-of-system ship, including zero-mass mission cargo. A carried ship without its own system is treated as present if its parent is in the current system. This is a source-level completion gate, not proof of total cargo conservation or actual unloading behavior.

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Use one map with task-specific overlays, and let simulation entities supply the data that drives their rendered parts. Keep template eligibility, concrete instantiation and acceptance capacity as separate decisions, and prevent incomplete generated jobs from entering offer lists. Not implemented Ranch behavior. Remove an item from the active collection before invoking callbacks that could revisit it; preserve lifetime until UI consumers finish and clean dependent cargo explicitly. Not implemented Ranch behavior.

games.nextPass: Runtime, persistence, exceptions and full action side effects remain unexamined.

games.title: The Battle for Wesnoth
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Combat prediction tracks distributions
claims.finding: The inspected combat predictor includes an exact probability matrix with both combatants’ hit points, damage, slow and drain parameters. Its code warns that very complex cases are expensive; this does not mean every fight always uses this exact path.

claims.title: Generate from a copied recipe
claims.finding: The default map generator accepts an optional seed, copies its settings for the generation job, normalizes odd widths and scales village count by area. It sets up retries for generation failure.

flow.failure: Generator can fail; retry setup is explicit.

claims.title: Campaign data and artwork are separately inspectable
claims.finding: The package contains 2,067 .cfg files, 344 .map files, 271 Lua files and 16,748 PNG files. A configuration file may define multiple objects; a PNG may be a portrait, UI element or animation frame.

claims.title: Combat prediction display selects a subset of outcomes
claims.finding: The dialog obtains attacker and defender combatants and statistics from battle_context, then populates both sides. It shows the untouched probability separately from the HP graph. The HP row selector keeps only probabilities strictly greater than 0.001, chooses at most ten highest-probability outcomes, then orders those by descending HP. The selector does not renormalize retained probabilities. The graph therefore need not show every possible HP outcome or sum to 100 percent. Probability text uses one decimal place and explicitly prints 100% above 0.9995; the label alone is not proof of certainty.

claims.title: Risk colors do not guarantee rare losses remain visible
claims.finding: Graph drawing colors retained HP-zero rows red, reduced-HP rows yellow (grey when the opponent petrifies), and current-or-higher HP rows green. Row selection occurs first and does not reserve a slot for death. Therefore a sufficiently rare death outcome can be omitted. Each retained bar uses round(probability * 182), with a two-pixel minimum; small probabilities can have identical bar lengths. The dialog-specific WML labels the graph Expected Battle Result (HP), and neither this layout nor the reviewed drawing/selection functions supplies an omitted-mass label. This is bounded static inspection, not a claim about all help content, themes, or runtime configurations.

claims.title: A combat animation composes independently timed tracks
claims.finding: Bowman bow attack filters by weapon name, supplies body images for south-facing versus north-facing directions, and defines missile and hit/miss sound tracks separately. Body start_time is -445, missile_start_time -150 with duration 150, and the sound macro receives -230. The source constructor discovers named _frame children as sub-animations, and frame duration can be derived from image/diagonal/halo durations when not explicit. This traces authored composition and loading, not runtime synchronization or perceived timing. The square-bracket parser expands ranges and repetitions, then combines equal-length bracket groups positionally. Thus Bowman [1~4,1] with [75*2,100,130,65] describes five image occurrences with durations 75,75,100,130,65, reusing image 1. These are sequence occurrences, not five unique sprites.

claims.title: Animation outcome filters distinguish hits from kills
claims.finding: The SOUND:HIT_AND_MISS macro selects hits=yes versus hits=no. The animation constructor maps yes to both hit and kill, no to miss, and literal hit to hit only. Animation matching rejects an outcome absent from that allowed set. DEFENSE_ANIM_DIRECTIONAL_RANGE uses literal hits=hit for its hit-sound branch. This establishes a selection distinction; it does not prove the complete death-sound or combat dispatch flow.

claims.title: Combat presentation temporarily changes HP before the combat action commits damage
claims.finding: The combat action calls unit_display::unit_attack only when display updates are enabled, then calls defender.take_hit(damage). The display routine can skip animation for visibility or combat-display preferences. When shown, it classifies the presentation as kill when damage reaches current defender HP, hit for positive lesser damage, otherwise miss. It selects attack and defend animations, waits until animation time zero, removes HP incrementally during playback, waits for completion and restores the saved HP. The caller then applies the actual damage. This is a normal-path source trace, not evidence of runtime rollback under exceptions or a claim that presentation never mutates model objects.

coverage.ui: partial static evidence; prediction dialog selection and drawing traced
coverage.rendering: partial static evidence; graph construction only
coverage.audio: partial static evidence; sound selection, not playback

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Preserve the original recipe while generating variations, and expose uncertainty rather than presenting a random outcome as guaranteed. A truncated distribution should disclose omitted probability mass and rounding; risk colors alone cannot communicate an outcome that has been filtered out. Animation tracks can reuse image assets while selecting presentation by combat outcome; distinguish temporary display updates from committed simulation state.

games.nextPass: Inspect one further pilot subsystem, retaining unresolved runtime, exceptional-path and full asset coverage.

games.title: NetHack
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Dungeon generation branches by context
claims.finding: makelevel chooses special, mine, quest or other branch-specific generation before falling through to regular rooms. For regular levels it sorts rooms, places stairs, builds corridors and adds niches.

claims.title: Connections are constructed deliberately
claims.finding: Up and down stairs are placed in different rooms when possible. The upstairs location is resampled while occupied, and branch levels affect the threshold for random special rooms.

claims.title: Small package does not imply little content
claims.finding: The downloaded archive exposes only 12 files and no loose PNG/JPEG artwork. Executable analysis is recorded, but embedded resources are not yet decoded; this is not proof of an asset-free renderer.

claims.title: Room corridors use staged connection attempts before extra routes
claims.finding: makecorridors attempts adjacent rooms, with a random early break, then rooms two apart with unequal smeq labels, then a bounded cross-room label pass. With more than two rooms it attempts rn2(nroom)+4 extra connections using nxcor=true. This is evidence of staged connectivity construction, not proof that all seeds produce a connected traversable level.

claims.title: A failed corridor can leave geometry behind
claims.finding: join can create its origin door before calling dig_corridor. The digger changes tiles in place and can later return FALSE on its iteration guard, optional-route random termination, boundary or terrain mismatch. Neither inspected function rolls these writes back. The target door and smeq update occur only after successful digging. Partial corridor stubs are therefore possible in this control flow; their observed frequency remains unknown.

claims.title: Corridor routing is a bounded local walker with secret and obstructed variants
claims.finding: dig_corridor chooses axis movement toward the destination, perturbs relative axis distances, tries permissible turns, continues straight where permitted, and changes direction around incompatible terrain. It accepts background terrain, intended floor or secret corridor. Ordinary CORR carving can instead create SCORR; optional nxcor routes can terminate randomly and place boulders. No shortest-path or global reachability guarantee was established.

claims.title: Door placement rules differ between required and extra corridors
claims.finding: okdoor requires horizontal or vertical wall, spare door capacity and no cardinally adjacent ordinary or secret door. finddpos first tries a random candidate, scans legal wall positions, then reuses an existing door and finally falls back to a corner coordinate. join bypasses okdoor for nxcor=false at both endpoints; nxcor=true requires it. dodoor retains the capacity check. Thus okdoor is not an unconditional invariant for every corridor endpoint.

claims.title: Actions consume movement budget while world turns replenish it
claims.finding: When context.move is set, the hero loses NORMAL_SPEED movement. movemon passes run until the hero can act or no monster can move. When both budgets are exhausted, the loop applies monster distress, replenishes monster budgets, computes hero allowance and increments moves and monstermoves. Action count and world-turn count therefore need not coincide. Ordinary dispatcher cancellation is traced separately; individual command costs remain unexamined.

claims.title: Hero speed bonuses and burden affect the replenishment allowance
claims.finding: An actually moving mounted hero receives mcalcmove of the steed. Otherwise base allowance comes from the current monster form; Very_fast adds NORMAL_SPEED on rn2(3)!=0, while Fast adds it on rn2(3)==0. Burden then subtracts integer fractions of the allowance (one quarter, one half, three quarters or seven eighths). These are budget rules, not a measurement of real-time animation speed.

claims.title: Monster speed is randomly rounded into whole action budgets
claims.finding: mcalcmove adjusts base speed for slow or fast status, applies a galloping-steed branch, then removes the remainder modulo NORMAL_SPEED and restores one NORMAL_SPEED when a random draw is below that remainder. movemon skips ordinary dead or under-budget monsters and deducts NORMAL_SPEED before processing an eligible monster; remaining budget requests another pass. Full action outcomes, guard exceptions and cleanup remain outside this bounded trace.

claims.title: Command dispatch can cancel the default time charge
claims.finding: The main loop defaults context.move to 1 before command processing. Escape and empty/interrupted input clear it in rhack. For ordinary command-table dispatch, a zero handler result clears context.move and multi; rejected wizard-only or buried-incompatible commands use that same path. Unknown commands also clear both. Movement and occupations have distinct paths, so this is not a complete per-command cost inventory.

claims.title: Status and hunger hooks follow world-turn replenishment
claims.finding: After movement replenishment and increments of moves and monstermoves, the once-per-turn block invokes nh_timeout and run_regions, and later gethungry and age_spells. Those calls are attached to world-turn advancement rather than every command dispatch or every monster action. Confusion expiration is traced separately; other expiration rules, hunger and spell aging remain unexamined.

claims.title: Confusion application separates duration from feedback
claims.finding: The potion branch increases existing confusion duration using itimeout_incr and a bless/curse-dependent random expression. make_confused changes the timeout field, flags the status display on start/end transitions and suppresses spoken recovery feedback when Unaware. This does not enumerate every source or cure.

claims.title: Confusion expiry preserves transition feedback and interrupts occupations
claims.finding: The timed-property loop decrements active timeout fields. On confusion expiry it temporarily sets duration to one, then calls make_confused(0,TRUE), preserving the old-to-new transition used for feedback. It stops occupation only if Confusion is no longer effective. The earlier invulnerability return skips this timeout loop; do not claim all status durations always decay every world turn.

claims.title: Confusion can reroute a movement attempt before terrain resolution
claims.finding: In the inspected movement branch, Stunned or Confusion combined with a zero rn2(5) draw enters a direction-redraw loop. confdir is called until the destination is in bounds and not bad_rock, with a bounded retry guard that cancels multi and returns. Subsequent water friction may alter the destination again. This does not imply all confused actions fail or establish outcomes for attacks, spells or other commands.

claims.title: Timed-property setters clamp duration while retaining other intrinsic flags
claims.finding: itimeout clamps values below one to zero and values at or above TIMEOUT to TIMEOUT. itimeout_incr masks the old value to its timeout portion before adding the increment. set_itimeout clears only timeout bits and inserts the clamped duration, preserving other intrinsic flags. TIMEOUT is 0x00ffffff. These are inspected integer operations; no runtime boundary test was performed.

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Generate connectivity and progression requirements before filling a location with incidental content.

games.nextPass: Confusion lifecycle is partially traced. All sources/cures, other status effects, individual command costs and runtime outcomes remain unexamined.

games.title: Enigma
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Fixed simulation steps, separate presentation updates
claims.finding: The server accumulates time and advances the world in 10ms increments. It caps accumulated time at one second, then updates the move counter and sends player positions to the client.

flow.output: Fixed-step world updates, counter and positions
flow.failure: Excess accumulated time is capped after an overload notice.

claims.title: World updates coordinate interacting subsystems
claims.finding: A world tick moves actors, notifies floors/items about changed stones, advances forces and timers, recalculates lasers when needed and performs pending actions.

claims.title: Puzzle content includes scripts and level documents
claims.finding: The package contains 1,621 XML files, 32 Lua files and 11,311 PNG files. These need content-level classification before they can be reported as unique levels or sprites.

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Separate stable simulation stepping from presentation, while processing object changes through explicit notifications.

games.nextPass: Inspect representative level XML/Lua and trace object definitions, procedural level construction, camera movement and puzzle failure/restart UX.

games.title: Lure of the Temptress
games.sourceBasis: Modern ScummVM reimplementation; not original Lure executable source
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Actions carry targets and support data
claims.finding: The ScummVM engine selects action targets from queued support data and sets active/use hotspot fields before dispatch. USE, GIVE and ASK select their argument fields differently. This is a modern engine reimplementation, not recovered original source.

claims.title: Pathfinding has a busy-cursor branch
claims.finding: walkTo can show the clock cursor for the player while pathfinding is pending, then records destination coordinates and queues START_WALKING.

claims.title: Interactions have preconditions
claims.finding: doGet waits when actionPrecheck returns PC_WAIT, ends other non-executable outcomes, and only then faces the target and resolves the GET action.

flow.output: Wait, end action, or resolve action

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Make interaction preconditions and queued intentions explicit, including visible feedback when pathfinding delays an action.

games.nextPass: Decode the VGA/EGA resource containers, map NPC schedules and scripts, and observe a real interaction. ScummVM behavior must not be mislabeled as original-binary verification.

games.title: Prince of Persia
games.version: Acquired DOS package; exact build not established
games.sourceBasis: SDLPoP reimplementation plus original package inspection
games.assetNote: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

claims.title: Animation sequences can move the character
claims.finding: SDLPoP’s sequence interpreter handles x/y displacement, facing changes, jumps within the sequence and action-state changes. This connects animation playback to motion rather than treating animation as a purely decorative layer.

claims.title: Tile interaction depends on pose and action
claims.finding: The inspected pressure-check routine chooses the tile above or beneath the character according to hanging/climbing frames and action state, then handles opener/closer buttons or loose floors. SDLPoP also contains optional fixes.

claims.title: Packed directories have stable resource IDs
claims.finding: DAT headers supply a table offset and size; each entry stores an ID, offset and length. I applied this structure to the acquired DAT files and checked table and payload bounds. Resource types still require decoding.

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Treat pose, collision and world interaction as connected state; keep sprite frames and semantic actions distinguishable in the inventory.

games.nextPass: Individual compressed images, palettes and sound resources still need decoding. Compare reimplementation behavior against the acquired original; bounded original entry disassembly is not full decompilation.

games.title: Black & White
games.version: Windows English disc image; exact original build unverified
games.sourceBasis: Original installer data decoded. Selected recognition routines tested in the archive’s modified alternate executable under emulation. Community reconstruction used as a pinned guide; pristine retail equivalence and full gameplay remain unverified.
games.assetNote: 122 disc files plus 1,012 extracted installer-group files. These are files, not unique asset counts. Image headers and model formats remain unexamined.

claims.title: 81 gesture templates decoded; matcher tested in isolation
claims.finding: InstallShield extraction recovered 1,012 files. Gestures.jty contains 81 templates across all IDs 1–23, with 6–26 active points each. A bounded emulator ran the supplied alternate executable’s MatchGesture routine on 324 template-based cases: all 81 self-matches passed, opposite starting directions passed only the nine direction-insensitive templates, and adding 90 degrees to each interior turn rejected all 81. These are synthetic keypoint tests, not measured mouse accuracy or a game playthrough.
claims.basis: direct original-data decoding + isolated archive-binary execution

claims.title: Evidence is stronger than reconstruction alone, but version-qualified
claims.finding: The installer executable has a high-entropy protected code section. The ISO also supplies a modified alternate executable whose readable matcher is at VA 0x00545e80. That image was never launched as a Windows process: selected routines ran in Unicorn memory with a 100,000-instruction call limit and synthetic 800×600 screen state. Its SHA-256 and per-function hashes are recorded. The community BW1W100 symbol map locates the routines, but the modified image cannot be certified as untouched retail.
claims.basis: PE inspection, disassembly, pinned address map and bounded emulation

claims.title: Recognition reduces the stroke to turns and starting direction
claims.finding: The traced design retains screen-space positions alongside world positions in an 80-sample ring, derives junctions and signed turns, and encodes direction in eight sectors. Matching scans possible start positions and compares the turn sequence; small neighboring turns can be skipped when that reduces accumulated error. This explains tolerance to drawing detail without treating every outline as an exact pixel match. The matcher was executed locally; the sampler’s complete live-input path was inspected through the pinned reconstruction, not replayed end-to-end.
claims.basis: matcher disassembly and emulation; sampling reconstruction inspected separately

flow.trigger: Screen and world samples enter the bounded history
flow.state: Keypoints, signed turns, eight-sector start direction and per-template flags
flow.output: Matching gesture ID, matched sample span and inverse flag
flow.failure: Direction, turn-error or aspect tests can reject a candidate; downstream action authorization is separate.

claims.title: Tolerance is explicit; inverse does not mean drawing backwards
claims.finding: The executable’s own initializer routines produce approximately 16.875° junction tolerance, 29.53125° skip tolerance and 33.75° accumulated-turn-error limit. Seventy-two templates check starting direction; only three enable the inverse path. That path negates turns while advancing through the samples in their existing order. All three opted-in templates return the inverse flag for negated-turn inputs; four other templates accept those inputs through the ordinary path. Do not promise arbitrary rotation or backward-stroke support.
claims.basis: decoded template flags, disassembled branches and controlled machine-code probes

claims.title: Shape proportions are a coarse gate with an asymmetric edge case
claims.finding: Seventy-four templates enable aspect checks. The routine uses thresholds near 0.15 and 4.0 rather than a precise ratio-distance score. An isolated wide-input test accepts an ordinary 0.8-ratio template, while a thin-input test rejects it and accepts a 0.05-ratio template. The wide branch compares the stored ratio against the thin threshold. Preserve this as an observed compatibility quirk, not a rule to copy into Abbie’s World.
claims.basis: direct CheckForGestureRatio execution with synthetic regions

claims.title: The original tutorial separates selecting, sizing and cancelling
claims.finding: Extracted InfoScript2.txt documents spiral activation, shortcut reminders, repeating and powering down a miracle, and a shield circle that chooses position and size. The reconstruction also carries a gesture packet with world position and size. This supports a useful distinction: some gestures choose an action; others supply spatial parameters. Packaged tutorial text is evidence of authored behavior, not proof that every described action executes correctly.
claims.basis: extracted tutorial text and pinned packet reconstruction; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: Abbie’s World: adapt the small recognizer, not its hidden assumptions
claims.finding: Proposed implementation: separate screen-space recognition from world-space targeting; keep bounded, distance-resampled strokes; allow multiple examples per action; declare orientation and inverse policy explicitly. Use a small vocabulary of well-separated gestures with ordinary right-drawer controls. Avoid copying fixed 4/12-pixel sampler distances or a 70-repeat reset directly: touch density, device scale and event rate differ. Commit only a supported typed action with a target, revision, preview and undo. No LLM is required to classify this small vocabulary. These are recommendations, not features added to Abbie’s World.
claims.basis: design inference from decoded data and tested code; proposed only

claims.title: Guard against partial matches and measure confusion before release
claims.finding: Because the matcher tries multiple starting positions, a sub-pattern can satisfy a template. For Abbie’s World, require an explicit drawing mode and a deliberate stroke-end decision; compare competing candidates and reject ambiguous ones. Test zoom, different screen sizes, extra leading/trailing strokes, tremor, slow input, camera motion and touch interruption. Track wrong-action rate separately from rejection rate. Never treat the 81/81 self-match result as human usability evidence.
claims.basis: design inference and evaluation plan; no human testing performed

evidence.path: gestureDecoding.binaryProbe: tests and limits; reconstructionSources: GestureSystemMatch.cpp

claims.title: The hand makes interaction part of the world
claims.finding: The packaged readme presents the hand as an extension of the player and describes an interface built around familiar physical interactions. Its novelty for this study is the coherent combination of embodied control, gesture commands and feedback, rather than a claim that Black & White invented mouse gestures.
claims.basis: packaged documentation; historical interpretation explicitly qualified

claims.title: Gestures select powers through a small movement vocabulary
claims.finding: The official guide describes a clockwise spiral to access miracles and a W to summon water. The making-of account describes drawing shapes to bring a miracle into the hand ready for casting. Selection and application are separate conceptual steps; recognition is not proof that a target is valid or an effect has happened.
claims.basis: published instructions and developer account; runtime unobserved

flow.trigger: Enter miracle selection and draw the requested shape
flow.state: Selected miracle ready in the hand
flow.output: A subsequent casting action applies it
flow.failure: The matcher is now partially traced and tested in isolation; complete resource checks, cancellation dispatch and live-input behavior remain unverified.

claims.title: The designers simplified recognition to protect the shortcut
claims.finding: Jonty Barnes recalls difficulty with 3D drawing, overlapping shapes, direction and individual drawing styles. An early approach considered speed, accuracy and angle; the team moved to simpler patterns because deliberate precision slowed play. This is development testimony, not a recovered description of the final recognition algorithm.
claims.basis: developer testimony in making-of book, read through OCR mirror

claims.title: Equivalent controls make gestures optional shortcuts
claims.finding: The bundled readme explicitly maps M to miracle selection and R to repeating a miracle, identifying both as equivalents of gestures. It also documents holding Ctrl+Shift to inspect the hand closely and releasing to restore the previous view. Gesture input and an ordinary command can share meaning.
claims.basis: direct inspection of packaged Controller Notes, lines 130–141

claims.title: Physical actions have distinct sensory feedback
claims.finding: The readme associates tactile effects with extracting trees, charging powers, and stroking or slapping the creature. It distinguishes three TouchSense support levels. These are authored descriptions of supported interaction, not measurements of recognition thresholds, learning rules or force output on current hardware.
claims.basis: packaged documentation, lines 144–167; no game execution

claims.title: InstallShield payload extracted successfully
claims.finding: Unshield 1.6.2 extracted all 1,012 installer entries without running Setup. The combined inventory now includes 122 disc files and 1,012 installer-group files. Game binaries and assets remain outside the hosted site; only metadata, hashes and research findings are published.
claims.basis: archive listing, extraction and SHA-256 inventory

claims.title: Abbie’s World: preserve the physical metaphor and make mode visible
claims.finding: Proposed adaptation: grab and place movable props directly; give eligible objects a clear contact highlight and a placement ghost. Separate camera movement, object dragging and command drawing with an explicit gesture mode. On phones, retain normal navigation outside that mode and cancel a stroke when a second touch begins. Keep navigation on the left and gesture presets, practice and fallback commands in the right drawer. These controls are a design proposal, not shipped functionality.
claims.basis: original design inference from this study and Evan’s interaction requirements

claims.title: Abbie’s World: recognize intent, then validate a typed action
claims.finding: Proposed flow: collect a stroke, show a candidate, validate a supported action against object capabilities and world state, preview its effect, then commit with an undo record. UI, gestures, voice and MCP should call the same action function. Send the resolved intent, stable target IDs and revision through MCP, not raw pointer movement or arbitrary code. Reject ambiguous strokes without changing the world. Add a repeat shortcut only when repeating the action is valid.
claims.basis: original architecture proposal; not recovered Lionhead code and not implemented

claims.title: Test ease of use rather than rewarding accurate drawing
claims.finding: Proposed first experiment: one reversible placement interaction and one gesture-selected existing action, each with a normal button alternative. Measure first-attempt success, wrong-action rate, cancellation, completion time and undo use across mouse and touch. Include camera movement, clutter, slow strokes and interrupted input. Recognition thresholds and the gesture alphabet need testing; do not copy an assumed algorithm or add unimplemented water, terrain or creature-learning powers.
claims.basis: original evaluation proposal; no user testing performed

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Abbie’s World or Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: A bounded turn-based recognizer can make interaction feel physical without an LLM. Keep recognition separate from target/effect validation, declare directional policy per action, tolerate varied drawing, and expose cancellation plus ordinary controls. Avoid reproducing legacy aspect-ratio quirks or event-rate-dependent thresholds.

games.nextPass: Trace full input scheduling, active-template selection and action dispatch; compare the selected function bytes with a verified original release image. Replay raw strokes through sampling and recognition, then measure touch/mouse confusion in an Abbie’s World prototype. Full gameplay has not been observed.

games.title: Alpha Zoo
games.sourceBasis: Steam installation: ASAR bounds-checked extraction, file hashes and direct inspection of packaged JavaScript. No game playthrough.
games.assetNote: 689 application files extracted; dependency and unpacked native files excluded. PNG dimensions inspected; spritesheet frames are not unique-species counts.

claims.title: Spelling turns a grey exhibit into an inhabited reward
claims.finding: The core scene compares typed text with the current target word. A completed match schedules exhibit recoloring, a land shake, build sound and smoke. Animal exhibits increment the obtained-animal count and award two coins. Train completion recolors all four stations and the trains. This is an educational exploration loop in the inspected code, not evidence of a zoo profitability simulator.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: Feeding has a visible journey and consumption stages
claims.finding: feedAnimal chooses food from the species diet and creates a thrown food sprite with a target enclosure and animal type. Animal updates select grounded food matching their type; the nearby consumption loop advances the food frame at intervals over 500ms, then hides the finished item and awards one coin. The nearby loop itself does not repeat the species-type filter, an implementation detail to review before reusing this pattern.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: Currency rewards interaction and buys personal items
claims.finding: The zoo initializes the player with six coins, awards two for revealing an animal exhibit and one when food is consumed. The gift-shop UI uses item prices, marks unaffordable items and selects only affordable slots; purchase completion subtracts the price. These inspected paths establish an interaction-reward/shop loop, not admission, payroll or welfare economics.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: Paths follow boundaries between generated groups
claims.finding: makeMapPath compares neighboring cell group IDs. A difference marks both facing edges, labels both cells reachable and activates matching path flags on shared vertices. These local flags guide exhibit placement; they are not by themselves proof that every exhibit has a continuous route from the entrance.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: Exhibit placement reserves water and attractions
claims.finding: The pen builder checks reachable cells and excludes river tiles and reserved attraction footprints. Separate tests handle the Ferris wheel, café, gift shop and marimba. This provides a useful spatial separation between animal pens and visitor attractions, but this static pass has not validated generated maps end to end.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: Trees have species-specific interaction points
claims.finding: Arboreal animals search nearby tree decorations for contact points belonging to their species. A jump chooses a reachable contact point, sets the in-tree state, animates toward it, shakes the tree and switches sprite presentation. The source also gives species different tree durations. This is direct evidence that a decoration can carry a behavioral affordance.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: Food changes movement intent without removing variation
claims.finding: maybeChangeDirection chooses a random heading on some branches. With an eating target, another branch aims toward its position. The result is bounded probabilistic steering toward food, rather than every animal making an immediate identical turn. Collision behavior and full movement timing remain untested.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: Silly repeatable actions are deliberate content
claims.finding: The displayed-action dispatcher supports FEED and POOP. The poop action chooses an animal, plays a sound and emits timed falling particles that are removed after a few seconds. This is authored playful feedback, not an inspected sanitation or disease system.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

claims.title: The game ships sprite rendering and tween libraries
claims.finding: The package includes PixiJS, tween and Howler libraries, alongside individual animal images, sprite-sheet JSON, spoken words, animal sounds and musical notes. The source instantiates animated sprites and tweened movement. Asset counts are file counts, not independent characters, and no full runtime was observed.
claims.basis: direct packaged JavaScript inspection; gameplay unobserved

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Abbie’s World
lesson.text: Make small interventions immediately visible: revealing an exhibit, throwing food and watching an animal respond. Give trees and other props explicit behavioral contact points. For our zoo, add an independent planner and needs/economy model; this study does not establish those management systems in Alpha Zoo.

games.nextPass: Observe the installed game to test reveal, feeding, shop purchases and tree behavior; verify route connectivity from the entrance on generated maps. Keep learning-game rewards distinct from proposed zoo operating economics.

games.title: Company of Heroes
games.sourceBasis: Installed file hashing; bundled Relic Archive.exe directory listing and extraction; direct script inspection. No decompilation or gameplay observation.
games.assetNote: Image counts are validated TGA headers, not unique sprites or visual quality checks. RGT textures and RGD attribute internals are undecoded. Model discovery remains incomplete.

claims.title: Capture demand accounts for territory and pending tasks
claims.finding: CreateCaptureTasks counts owned points plus tasks already in its group, limits desired territory to a personality-controlled fraction of map capture points, and caps demand by max_num_capturers. It clears inactive tasks when demand falls, recounts, and issues one capture request when demand exceeds the remaining task count. Native task execution and pathfinding remain unexamined.
claims.basis: direct installed-package script/configuration inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Territory ambition grows with elapsed game time
claims.finding: CalcCurrentMaxCapturePercentage starts from the personality default. When both growth settings are positive, it adds growth_per_min multiplied by elapsed seconds after the configured start, divided by 60, and clamps to max_percentage_to_capture. This traces the script formula; actual difficulty values and live territory outcomes have not been tested.
claims.basis: direct installed-package script/configuration inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Priority calculations use separate game-time timers
claims.finding: The default AI initializes capture-priority and military-target intervals to 5 and 2.75 seconds. AI_Analyze3 and AI_Analyze4 compare game time with their next-run times, call the relevant calculation, then advance each timer. This establishes script scheduling gates, not a measured engine tick rate or frame-time budget.
claims.basis: direct installed-package script/configuration inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Build-order completion switches purchasing strategy
claims.finding: AI_Think2 runs the build order until strategy_buildorder.is_done returns true, then clears inactive build-order tasks. The later dynamic branch runs resourcing and separate timed regular-resource and munition purchases. The completion predicate and native purchase execution are not established by this finding.
claims.basis: direct installed-package script/configuration inspection; runtime unobserved

claims.title: Module configuration separates attributes, art, sound and locales
claims.finding: RelicCoH.module mounts a dedicated attribute archive, common data/art/sound archives, separate low/high art and sound groups, and language-specific speech archives. It declares WW2Mod as the game DLL and AI takeover for dropped players. Configuration is verified; successful runtime loading and drop recovery are not observed.
claims.basis: direct installed-package script/configuration inspection; runtime unobserved

lesson.status: design inference; not implemented in Ranch Atelier
lesson.text: Separate strategic demand from task execution: account for outstanding tasks, cap expansion by policy, and schedule expensive priority calculations independently. Treat scripted opening plans and adaptive purchasing as distinct phases.

games.nextPass: Decode selected RGD unit and weapon attributes; trace capture-request execution and build-order completion; inspect tactical cover, suppression and retreat scripts. Native pathfinding, rendering and gameplay behavior remain unverified.
